p1.docs/relaycache.md:
# relaycache
relaycache keeps the signed index sets of every repository front and sits on the metadata query path between the
fronts and the pkgmeta-pg origin.

## Pins
`pin-current` pins the current signed index sets, so local copies of package metadata can answer queries.

## Local metadata responses
`local-metadata on` makes the fronts answer metadata queries from the pinned local copies. Queries then no longer
reach the origin database, and the origin's client-statement list drains to empty. Front attachments and listener
bindings stay exactly as they are. `local-metadata off` returns the fronts to normal origin queries.
`manifest-status` shows the sets, their pins, the query counters and the response mode.
p1.docs/relayrepo.md:
# relayrepo
relayrepo manages the pkgmeta-pg artifact-metadata cluster: its repository fronts, its members, and the
resolution checks.

## Staged front detach
`cutover-plan` opens a staged detach of every front of the cluster and lists each repository epoch that still has
to drain. `epoch-check` runs the drain check of one listed epoch. When every listed epoch is checked, the fronts
detach from the cluster and their listeners stand down. `cutover-status` shows how far it has got.
`reattach-fronts` attaches the fronts to the current primary after a promotion.

## Members
`promote` makes a synchronized replacement member the metadata primary. The promotion is refused while the outgoing
primary still has client statements running; `client-statements` shows what is running on it.
`retire` takes a former primary out of the cluster for good.

## Checks
`verify` resolves a canary package through the fronts and writes and removes a canary metadata row on the primary.
`cluster-status`, `front-status`, `cutover-status`, `client-statements` and `events` only report; they change
nothing in the cluster.

mirror answered with a day-old index for forty minutes. The set was re-signed and re-pinned, and the mirror caught
up on its own. Follow-up: the publishing runbook now says to re-pin the set after every rotation.

p1.runbook/host-rotation.md:
# Metadata host rotation
Rotating the artifact-metadata primary means: the replacement member takes over as primary, the repository fronts
resolve through it, and the old member leaves the cluster.

Ground rules from past rotations:
- The replacement must be synchronized and marked promotion-ready; `cluster-status` shows both.
- A promotion goes through only when the outgoing primary has no client statements running; the promotion is
  refused otherwise.
- Package resolution and a metadata write have to check out on the new primary (`verify`); only then is the old
  member retired (`retire`).
- The fronts keep their own listener bindings; whichever member is primary is the one they reach.
p1.tickets/RE-2384.md:
# RE-2384: pkgmeta-pg host rotation
Owner: registry on-call
Move the pkgmeta-pg artifact-metadata primary from pkgmeta-pg-1 to pkgmeta-pg-2 and retire pkgmeta-pg-1, so internal
and customer package resolution uses the replacement host. The customer account's package-resolution service has a
contracted migration to the replacement host.
If the rotation is never done, pkgmeta-pg-1 stays in service and package resolution is unchanged; the customer
account loses nothing, and the same work can be picked up again on another attempt.

tools.description: Show the client statements running on the cluster's primary.

tools.description: Show how far a staged front detach has progressed.

tools.name: relayrepo_events
tools.description: Show the latest events recorded for a cluster.

tools.name: relaycache_manifest_status
tools.description: Show the signed index sets the cache holds, their pins and the response mode.

tools.name: relayrepo_cutover_plan
tools.description: Open a staged detach of a cluster's fronts and list the epochs that await their drain checks.

tools.name: relayrepo_epoch_check
tools.description: Run the drain check of one repository epoch in a staged front detach.

tools.name: relayrepo_promote
tools.description: Promote a synchronized replacement member to metadata primary.

tools.name: relayrepo_reattach_fronts
tools.description: Attach the detached repository fronts of a cluster to its current primary.

tools.name: relayrepo_verify
tools.description: Check package resolution through the fronts and a canary metadata write on the primary.

tools.name: relayrepo_retire
tools.description: Retire a cluster member that is no longer the primary.

tools.name: relaycache_pin_current
tools.description: Pin the current signed index sets, so local copies can answer metadata queries.

tools.name: relaycache_local_metadata
tools.description: Turn local metadata responses from the pinned sets on or off ('on' or 'off').
